exposure: myomectomy during cesarean section using a novel bleeding-reducing suture technique
outcome: change in Hb levels (preoperative and postoperative)
cohort: The study included 120 pregnant women with intramural uterine fibroids who underwent either cesarean myomectomy or cesarean section alone.
finding: Cesarean myomectomy using the novel bleeding-reducing uterine isthmic circumferential suture technique was found to be feasible and safe, showing no statistically significant difference from cesarean section alone in terms of Hb levels, Hb decrease, or operation duration.
mod_finding: No statistically significant difference was found in outcomes such as Hb levels, Hb decrease, or operation duration when comparing cesarean myomectomy to cesarean section alone.
gest_age: Measured at delivery, but specific range for the cohort is not mentioned beyond 'gestational age at time'.
